text: Shein raised $1.74B in its Hong Kong IPO at a $26.5B valuation, versus $100B privately in 2022. Shares fell 9% on debut. 2025 revenue was $41.8B; Q1 2026 revenue was $9.05B with a $99M net loss.

meta.note: Public listing exposes a market valuation after prior New York and London listing attempts did not materialize.

text: The 10-year Treasury yield reached its highest level since Jan. 14, 2025, trading at 4.788%. The 30-year stood at 5.261% and the 2-year at 4.385%. WTI traded above $89 and Brent above $94 as U.S. strikes in Iran and disruption around Hormuz remained active.

meta.note: The event combines elevated sovereign yields with contemporaneous oil-price and geopolitical pressure.

text: Fed Governor Michael Barr said he would support raising rates if inflation does not moderate sufficiently. The federal funds target remains 3.5%-3.75%. Barr supported the July hold, while headline inflation stands at 3.7% and core inflation at 3.3%.

meta.note: The rate-increase position is explicitly conditional rather than an adopted FOMC policy stance.

text: U.S. forces struck IRGC targets around the Strait of Hormuz following attempted attacks on commercial shipping and U.S. personnel. Iran subsequently reported missile and drone operations targeting U.S. bases and interests in the region.

meta.note: Reported target counts, strike locations, and U.S. military assets were not disclosed.

text: WTI reached $90.03 per barrel, its highest level since July 24, while Brent traded at $94.52. Commercial shipping attacks and direct U.S.-Iran strikes remain active around the Strait of Hormuz, a major global oil transit corridor.

meta.note: Military activity and oil pricing coexist in the event; the Text does not assign causal direction.

text: Dell reported $46.97B in quarterly revenue, up 58% YoY. Infrastructure Solutions revenue reached $31.78B, including $16.40B from AI-optimized servers. Dell raised FY2027 revenue guidance to $192B and AI-server sales guidance to $74B.

meta.note: Infrastructure and client businesses remain within the same reporting structure despite sharply different growth rates.
